decisive_moments.reason: Con identified the central policy ambiguity: valuing reproducibility more than novelty is stronger than requiring adequate verification, and the former may distort the research portfolio.

Pro effectively addressed the truth-versus-reproducibility objection and distinguished individual incentives from system-level knowledge quality, but mainly asserted that portfolio protections could solve the opportunity cost.

Con directly returned to the comparative burden and explained why reproducibility is not a proxy for importance, validity, or truth, while arguing that reserving some discovery funding may not prevent distortion.

flags.quote: Institutions can address opportunity cost by reserving funding for high-risk discovery, while giving greater weight to reproducible methods
reproducibility determines which deserve cumulative investment
If reproducibility is the dominant criterion, researchers rationally avoid questions whose methods, data, or effects are initially difficult to verify
